name: NetworkEventSystem
summary: Client side of the UDP game-server connection. Owns the transport object (+0x10, 0x350 bytes). Each frame it pumps the transport, then sends the queued connection events (connect, disconnect, packet received and so on) to its virtual handlers. Received game packets are demultiplexed by channel to registered channel handlers (list at +0x20), which read entity ids and bitstreams.
tick: Reads the 'disableTimeout' cvar; takes the transport lock (+0x150) and calls UdpTransport_Tick; splices the transport event queue (+0x238) and sends each event by type: 1 goes to vfunc 0x88 (__HandleConnectEvent), 2 to 0x98, 3 to 0x90, 4 to 0xa0 (packet received), 5 to 0xa8. It then frees the event buffers and calls vfunc 0x80, which copies net stats (ping/RTT, a 0xe0-byte stats block) into globals and the netgraph object from FUN_7ff650c2c410 when the game EA state is 4.
callbacks: OnInitialize allocates and constructs the transport (FUN_7ff650e31640) and stores the local port/id at +0x38. PreDelete tears it down.
interacts_with: EA entity-id hash (EA+0x10) to resolve entity ids in packets
registered per-channel packet handlers (+0x20 list, vfuncs +0x30/+0x38)

key_functions.0x7ff650c4fd40: vfunc 0x88 __HandleConnectEvent: reset stats, broadcast connect, notify channel handlers
key_functions.0x7ff650c500a0: vfunc 0xa0 packet received: frame-time stats; type 1 = per-entity bitstream sent to channel handlers, type 0xf = raw sent to the last handler
key_functions.0x7ff650c4f7f0: vfunc 0x80 post-tick: copy net stats into globals/netgraph

server_relevance: Client-only (client end of the transport). The server needs the matching peer protocol: a connect handshake, then type-1 packets with an entity-id bitstream for each channel.
evidence: Strings 'NetworkEventSystem_C::__HandleConnectEvent', '::__Disconnected', '::DisconnectFromInstance'. Calls UdpTransport_Tick. Handles event types 1-5. 'disableTimeout' cvar.

name: MirrorSystem (replication receive)
summary: Applies received replication (Mirror) messages to the ECS: create, update or destroy networked entities. It also triggers one-time local-player setup once the local player entity exists, and runs integrity (anti-tamper) CRC checks on code pages.
tick: Gets the local player entity id (FUN_7ff650bfd2f0). Calls FUN_7ff650bff690, which does a random CRC32 check of one 4 KB code page against a table (DAT_7ff6517fd478) and reports a mismatch. It then drains the queued replication batches (+0x98/+0xa0) through FUN_7ff650bffdf0: op 1 = create entity (FUN_7ff650c00d20), op 2 = update existing entity (FUN_7ff650c00560), op 3 = destroy (FUN_7ff650c00c80). When the local player entity first resolves (flag +200), it runs a one-time init (FUN_7ff650c19340). There is also a 500 ms tick-count anti-debug check.
components_written: many (component state deserialized from mirror data)

key_functions.0x7ff650bff690: code-page CRC check + drain replication batches
key_functions.0x7ff650bffdf0: per-batch op dispatch (1 create / 2 update / 3 delete)

server_relevance: Client-only receiver. The server must produce the matching create/update/delete mirror stream. This is the core of server-to-client entity sync.
evidence: Already identified as the replication/Mirror system. Op switch 1/2/3 on 0x14-byte records, each with an entity id and a per-entity bitreader (+0x170).

name: PlayerPawnLinkSystem (controller <-> hero link)
summary: Keeps the two-way link between a player/controller entity and the hero entity it controls. Component 0x20 on the player entity holds the hero entity id at +0x78. Component 0x1F on the hero holds the owning player id at +0x18. The system also keeps the local-player component 0x2F 'controlled entity' (+0x1520) in sync.
tick: (1) Retries pending links (list +0x10/+0x18 of {heroId, playerId}): once the hero entity exists, writes 0x1F.+0x18 = playerId and removes the entry. (2) Iterates component 0x2F (local player). Compares the entity id at +0x1520 with the pawn resolved through FUN_7ff650cd3f40. On a change, calls FUN_7ff650ce7590 to re-possess: sets the old pawn's owner to invalid and the new pawn's owner to this player, updates +0x1520, resets fields in the new pawn's 0x1F, and flags the viewmodel/camera dirty (0x200).
callbacks: OnInitialize registers two field-change callbacks for component 0x20 on the EA callback registry (EA+0x198). On add (FUN_7ff650c089f0) it caches the player id and pawn id. On change (FUN_7ff650c08a40) it unlinks the old hero's 0x1F owner, links the new one (or queues it if the hero does not exist yet), and calls FUN_7ff650ce7830. OnEntityRemoved clears the links when an entity with 0x1F or 0x20 goes away.
server_relevance: Client-side derived state. The server only needs to replicate component 0x20 (player -> hero id) correctly; the client rebuilds the reverse link itself.
evidence: Subscribes to 0x1f/0x20. The 0x20 field +0x78 entity id is mirrored into 0x1F+0x18 of that entity. 0x2F+0x1520 is updated with the pawn entity id. Component 0x20 is defined on the player def 0x0e and 0x1F on def 0x3cf.

name: CollisionProxySyncSystem (component 0x16)
summary: Small system (0x18 bytes) with no OnTick. It exposes a secondary interface at +0x10 whose method iterates component 0x16 (deps 0x01, 0x12). For each one it pushes the entity's movement-state position (0x12 component +0xa280, transformed by the +0xa060 matrix) into a physics/collision body handle, then updates that body's collision filter from the team/filter bits (component 0x10).
tick: No OnTick. The per-frame work is in the secondary interface method FUN_7ff650c7f4a0, called by an external update list rather than the system tick loop.
interacts_with: physics world handle table DAT_7ff6517f8a20 (FUN_7ff6511bb2f0 set position, FUN_7ff6511ba590/FUN_7ff651197370 collision filter 0x1081/0x1099)

key_functions.0x7ff650c7f4f0: sync body position from movement state + update team collision filter

server_relevance: Probably needed server-side in some form (hit/collision proxies follow movement). As written, it is client physics glue.
evidence: Component list 0x210/0x18=0x16. Reads component mask bit 0x12 at +0xa280. Handle-based world table with a 0x50-byte body stride. Filter words 0x1081/0x1099 chosen by team. Component 0x16 has 0 instances in current dumps, so the purpose is unconfirmed.

name: ProjectileNetworkReceiveSystem
summary: Large multi-interface system (about 0x3e8 bytes, a message-dispatcher base with about 21 handler registries) with no OnTick. Its network-channel interface (at +0x390) parses bitstream messages for projectiles. Snapshots go into the projectile component 0x27 history (+0x6c0 list of 0x180-byte states keyed by frame). Spawns for projectiles whose entity does not exist yet are buffered in the singleton component 0x70 (0xc0-byte records with a 600-frame timeout).
tick: No OnTick. Work happens when the network layer calls the channel handler FUN_7ff650c15610.

key_functions.0x7ff650c15610: channel handler: sends to both parsers when the entity is valid
key_functions.0x7ff650d21e90: parse projectile-spawn records into component 0x70 pending list (+0xc0), timeout 600
key_functions.0x7ff650d16540: parse projectile state snapshot (frame = two varints); insert into 0x27 history or the 0x70 buffered list (0x4b0 frames); rewind state (FUN_7ff650d19a80)

server_relevance: Client-only receiver. The server must send projectile spawn/state messages on this channel if projectiles are server-authoritative.
evidence: Ctor FUN_7ff650be2840 sets 5 vtables (+0,+0x388..+0x3a0) with base FUN_7ff650fef8d0. Iterates 0xa80/0x18 = component 0x70. Uses component mask bit 0x27 (STUProjectileComponent) with snapshot arrays keyed by frame number.

name: ProjectileSystem (simulation + interpolation)
summary: Runs projectile simulation for all projectile components (0x27) on command-frame boundaries, splitting the work into parallel jobs. It then interpolates projectile visuals every frame using the command-frame fraction.
tick: Computes the frame fraction (accumulated time / 16000 µs, i.e. one 16 ms CF). When a new CF is due, iterates component 0x27: projectiles that are simple or already initialized are stepped inline (vtable 0x7ff6515a3048 slot 2, updating velocity +0xc0 and last position +0xaf0), and the rest are gathered and simulated in parallel jobs (FUN_7ff650c131d0). Every frame a second pass over 0x27 does visual interpolation (FUN_7ff650d17030 / FUN_7ff650d17230 with alpha * timescale).
interacts_with: job system (parallel split by DAT_7ff651872130 workers)
server_relevance: Server-side game logic (projectile simulation and hits) plus client visuals. The simulation part is needed on a server.
evidence: Iterates EA+0xb0+0x3a8 (component 0x27 = STUProjectileComponent). Divides by 16000.0 (16 ms CF in µs). Splits work into parallel jobs. Stores velocity and last-position fields.

name: CameraSystem
summary: Computes the local player's camera each frame: first-person camera, animation contribution, near-Z override, combat/UX outlines, and gamepad camera inertia/stick power. Pushes the result to the renderer view.
tick: If camera updates are enabled (camera_EnableUpdate), gets the view object (EA vfunc 0xe8), the local player (FUN_7ff650c3b110) and the controlled pawn (FUN_7ff650c3b860), and sets the camera target/first-person info (FUN_7ff650beb650). Sets FP animation effect, computes the camera (FUN_7ff650bebb70 / FUN_7ff650bebc20), on a reset flag resets the camera smoothing of all component 0x1F instances (+0x128), then writes the final view to the render view (FUN_7ff650be9c70 / FUN_7ff650bea510).
callbacks: OnEntityAdded (component 0x22 STUFirstPersonComponent) binds the camera target when appropriate (FUN_7ff650c3e8e0 gate).

key_functions.0x7ff650bea8e0: OnInitialize: registers cvars camera_EnableUpdate, camera_FirstPersonAnimationEffect, camera_FirstPersonNearZ, camera_combatOutlines, camera_uxOutlines, camera_gamePadCameraDampening, camera_useGamePadCameraDampening, camera_gamepadStickPower, camera_gamepadTriggerPower
key_functions.0x7ff650beb650: set camera target entity / FP mode

evidence: Cvar strings 'Enable camera update', 'camera_FirstPersonNearZ', 'camera_combatOutlines', 'Gamepad camera inertia dampening'. Subscribes to STUFirstPersonComponent (0x22).

name: VoiceLineSystem (voice stimuli + conversations)
summary: Plays hero voice lines. Queued voice stimuli (0x70-byte records: source entity, target entity, stimulus GUID...) are resolved against the speaker's STUVoiceSetComponent (0x46). The system applies probability and cooldown timers and team-relation rules (friendly/enemy/any, local-player involvement, pets 0x3d), plays the line, and can trigger multi-hero voice conversations loaded from a resource list.
tick: Decrements the voice cooldown timers (FUN_7ff65102c310). Sends the queued conversation triggers (+0xd8 list, 0x28 each) to vfunc 0xa8 (FUN_7ff650c20350: conversation eligibility checks, then pick participants). Refreshes participant entity ids for active conversations (FUN_7ff650c1ff60). Continues active conversations (FUN_7ff650c1e320). Then vfunc 0x70 (FUN_7ff65102c530) processes the stimulus queue: dedupe, probability roll vs threshold +0x74, fetch voice set from component 0x46, choose a line (vfunc 0x88/0x90), play it (vfunc 0x78), and possibly raise a conversation (vfunc 0xa8).
callbacks: OnInitialize registers message/handler type 99 (FUN_7ff6509a7f20). Loads resource 0x46000000000002b (a list of conversation definitions) into the sorted table at +0xc0. PreDelete releases them.
server_relevance: Mostly client presentation (audio). The server may need to send stimulus events, but no server logic depends on this.
evidence: Uses component mask +0xa0 bit 6 = component 0x46 (STUVoiceSetComponent) and 0x3d STUPetComponent. Random roll vs float threshold, cooldown timers, team relation mode 0/1/2 at +0x7c.

name: MapWorldSystem (map scene load/tick)
summary: Owns the loaded map/world scene objects (+0xb0 and +0x18, destroyed with FUN_7ff6509b74f0). Ticks them every frame, which drives map streaming/loading and scene time. It also indexes map-placed entities by their placement GUID and syncs component 0x10 filter bits into the scene component (0x01). This is the system that spawns map entities during map load.
tick: Once either world's load state (+0x3a8 -> +0x160) reaches 4 (loaded) and the global flag is set, marks loaded (+0xeb). Calls FUN_7ff6509d6770(world, dt) for both worlds: time scaling (+0x3d8), load-step while not loaded, per-object updates, and a renderer notify (DAT_7ff6517fe3e0 vfunc 0x4f8) when loaded.
callbacks: OnInitialize registers a component-0x10 change callback (FUN_7ff650c246e0) that copies the 48-bit filter mask into scene component +0x1b8 and marks it dirty 0x200. It also creates the helper at +0xb8 and the object at +0x70. OnEntityAdded (FUN_7ff65102eaf0): for entities with component 0x06, reads the GUID from comp+8 and stores GUID -> entity id in the map at +0x48. PreDelete destroys the worlds and releases the map resource (+0xc8).

key_functions.0x7ff65102eaf0: OnEntityAdded: index map entities by GUID

server_relevance: Needed in some form server-side (map load and the map-entity GUID -> id index used for spawning and referencing map objects). Rendering parts are client-only.
evidence: Brief notes that system 43 spawns map entities. Load-state==4 checks. World tick with time scale. GUID->entity map. Filter bits copied to scene +0x1b8.

name: GameHUDSystem (HUD entity + UI input actions)
summary: Makes sure a singleton HUD/UI entity exists: it spawns it from the definition returned by vfunc 0x80 and sends Statescript identifier 0x5800000000000dc to it on creation. It also routes certain input actions to the lobby/UI layer: action 0xab opens a UI screen or shows a message depending on PvP game mode, and action 0xb1 is gated by a Statescript identifier on the local hero.
tick: If the tracked entity id (+0x18) no longer resolves, respawns it (vfunc 0x70 = FUN_7ff650d14e10) and pokes its Statescript (FUN_7ff650c12a30, component 0x23). If input action 0xab is pressed (FUN_7ff650cccc40), runs FUN_7ff650d15160 (checks component 0x3F / 0x24 PvPGame mode 0xd80000000000018, then UI event 0x0a4.../0x024...7b or a localized message). Tracks two booleans from the lobby UI object and flags the view dirty (0x1000000) on change. In the main game EA, reads the local player -> 0x20 -> hero -> 0x23 Statescript and checks identifier 0x5800000000001cf plus action 0xb1, then sends UI event {0x40000, 0x7c4} (FUN_7ff65101b800).
evidence: Input action bytes at +0x454. UI manager accessed via DAT_7ff651813e18 vfunc 0xe0. Statescript identifier GUIDs (type 0x058). Spawns an entity when missing.

name: BattleNetLoginSystem
summary: Lobby-side Battle.net authentication state machine (object 0x498 bytes, stored at lobby EA+0x178). Drives the login connection, processes auth web responses (auth GET/POST parsing, captcha, legal acceptance), and reports login errors and timeouts through localized error strings.
tick: If the login-requested flag is set, pumps the connection (FUN_7ff6510c5c50 loop). Processes the queued auth results under a lock (FUN_7ff6510bf790): case 0 error, 1 Parse Auth Get (state 6), 2 Show Captcha (state 8/7), 3 Parse Auth Post (state 0xe), 4 Set Legal (state 0xb), 5 success/reset. Resets the connection when needed (FUN_7ff6510b5030) and raises 'Timed out trying to login to battle.net' (0xde0000000001bb3) on timeout.
callbacks: OnInitialize sets a global 'lobby ready' flag under a critical section. PreDelete clears it.
interacts_with: lobby UI error display (localized strings type 0x0de)

key_functions.0x7ff6510b5960: raise login error with localized string

server_relevance: Login flow only. Not needed by a match server (must be bypassed or emulated for the client to reach the game).
evidence: Strings 'Timed out trying to login to battle.net', 'Invalid state for Parse Auth Get/Post', 'Invalid state for Show Captcha', 'Invalid state for Set Legal'.

name: LobbyDelayedUIEventSystem
summary: Small lobby system (0x70 bytes, lobby EA+0x1b8) holding two record lists (+0x18 and +0x58) that its secondary interface clears. Its OnTick runs a one-shot 5-second timer: when armed (+0x33), it accumulates dt and after 5.0 s posts UI event 0x240000000000098 through the lobby UI manager.
tick: If +0x33 is set: +0x38 += dt; if > 5.0 s, clears the flag and calls FUN_7ff650c24dd0(0x240000000000098) to post a UI event/screen. Includes the usual anti-tamper stub.
callbacks: Secondary interface (vtable +0x70 region) FUN_7ff650c67130 frees two lists of 0x90-byte records (+0x18) and another list (+0x58).
evidence: Constant at 0x7ff65160cf58 = 5.0. Only action is posting a UI event with GUID 0x240000000000098. What arms +0x33 was not traced.

name: LobbyPlayerResourceWatchSystem (game-EA component 0x35 hook)
summary: One-shot lobby system. On its first tick it registers a field-change callback on the game EA's component 0x35 (player entity def 0x0e). When field hash 0x12ab923c changes, the callback reloads the resource handle at comp+0xa0 from the GUID at comp+0x90. It also has handler code (FUN_7ff650c092c0) that forwards events to the game EA (+0x1d0) or lobby (+0x138) handlers depending on the lobby state (6/5).
tick: If not yet registered (+0x10 == 0): set the flag, then call (*(gameEA+0x198))->vfunc 0x10(callback 0x7ff650c091e0, componentId 0x35). Nothing afterwards.
callbacks: Callback 0x7ff650c091e0: if the changed field hash is 0x12ab923c, releases the old resource handle at +0xa0 and acquires a new one for the GUID at +0x90.
interacts_with: game EA (DAT_7ff651797f90) component callback registry EA+0x198

key_functions.0x7ff650c09280: OnTick (not a Ghidra function; read from live bytes)

server_relevance: Client-side resource loading. The server only has to replicate the component 0x35 GUID field.
evidence: Live disassembly: mov r8b,0x35; jmp [vtbl+0x10] on gameEA+0x198. Callback compares field hash 0x12ab923c (unresolved) and reloads the resource at +0x90 -> +0xa0.

name: LobbyNotificationTimeoutSystem (component 0x74)
summary: Tiny lobby system. Each tick it reads the first lobby component 0x74 (singleton, 0x2f8 bytes) and clears its timestamp field +0x208 once more than 5000 ms have passed, i.e. it expires a transient lobby state or notification.
tick: FUN_7ff650c29670 -> first component 0x74 of the lobby EA (DAT_7ff651813e18+0xb0+0xae0). If +0x208 != 0 and now_ms - +0x208 > 5000, set +0x208 = 0.
evidence: 0xae0/0x18 = 0x74. Millisecond clock (DAT_7ff65177f0f0 * scale). 5000 threshold. The meaning of component 0x74 is unknown.
